gauntlet: question
A fits the current code because the setting has a single owner. `settings/resolver.ts:12` already owns the defaults, and `ui/report-view.ts:30` already consumes the resolved values. I traced that path end to end, and existing settings already flow through it. Adding the new key there means one read path and one place for defaults, and the view needs no new loading code. A view-local settings object would be a second settings path beside the resolver. Its defaults could drift from the resolver's, and every later report setting would have to choose between the two. I've noted ownership as decided: the setting is a key under the existing resolver.

The next open point is what happens to active report filters when the workspace changes. Today they stay active, and that can hide rows in the new workspace. Which behavior should the setting control?
A) Reset filters on a workspace change by default. The setting lets users opt back into keeping them.
B) Keep filters by default, as today. The setting lets users opt into resetting them.
C) Remember filters per workspace. Switching restores that workspace's own last filters instead of carrying the previous workspace's filters over.
D) other - name it
Recommendation: A - it fixes the reported hidden-row problem for everyone by default, and users who rely on filters carrying over keep that behavior through the resolver key.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
gauntlet: question
Reusing the resolver fits because `settings/resolver.ts:12` already owns defaults, and `ui/report-view.ts:30` already consumes its resolved settings. The traced path can carry the new setting without creating a second settings object whose defaults could drift from the shared ones.

What should the setting’s default behavior be when switching workspaces?
A) Reset report filters by default, with an option to retain them.
B) Retain report filters by default, with an option to reset them.
C) other - name it.
Recommendation: A - it addresses rows being unexpectedly hidden in a new workspace while preserving an explicit way to retain filters.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Both outputs explain why the shared resolver fits the supplied code (resolver.ts:12 owns defaults, report-view.ts:30 consumes resolved values, the path is already used) and retain choice A, so f1 holds in both. Both also continue in the same response with one labeled-options question on the undecided reset behavior, each with an explicit Recommendation line, without stopping at acknowledgment or launching into approaches, so f2 holds in both. After adds a third concrete option (C, remember filters per workspace) and an explicit 'noted ownership as decided' sentence, which do not move either fact; the only mild risk in After is that option C introduces a design variant not grounded in gathered evidence, so if you want to keep the question tightly scoped to the undecided reset behavior, keep the two-option-plus-other form of Before while retaining After's clearer single-owner explanation and its ownership-recorded sentence.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Both outputs keep f1 and f2: each explains the resolver fit from the supplied `settings/resolver.ts:12` / `ui/report-view.ts:30` evidence, then asks one labeled A/B/C question with an own-line Recommendation about the undecided reset behavior rather than stopping at acknowledgment or launching approaches. The one soft spot in After is that it dropped Before's explicit sentence ("I'll carry your choice forward as the ownership decision; it does not yet decide filter-reset behavior"), so retention of choice A is now only implicit in the explanation; a stricter reader of f1 could hesitate. To keep every fact robustly while delivering the Change, keep a short explicit carry-forward line after the rationale (e.g., "Carrying A forward as the ownership decision; it does not decide filter reset, which is the next question.") before the labeled options — this costs one sentence and makes both the retained choice and the still-open reset decision unambiguous in the output text.
